questions.q: The natural frequency of an $L-C$ circuit is $1,25,000 \mathrm{cycle} / \mathrm{s}$. Then the capacitor $C$ is replaced by another capacitor with a dielectric medium of dielectric constant $K$. In this case, the frequency decreases by $25 \mathrm{kHz}$. The value of $K$ is

$f=\frac{1}{2 \pi \sqrt{L C}}$
or
$f \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{C}}$
When capacitor $C$ is replaced by another capacitor $C^{\prime}$ of dielectric constant $K$, then
$\begin{gathered}C^{\prime}=K C \\ \frac{f^{\prime}}{f}=\sqrt{\frac{C}{C^{\prime}}} \\ \frac{125000-25000}{125000}=\sqrt{\frac{C}{K C}} \\ \frac{100}{125}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{K}} \\ K=\left(\frac{125}{100}\right)^2=1.56\end{gathered}$

questions.q: An oscillating circuit consisting of a capacitor with capacitance $C=10 \mu \mathrm{F}$, a coil with inductance $L=6.0 \mu \mathrm{H}$ and active resistance $R=10 \Omega$. The mean power that should be fed to the circuit to maintain undamped harmonic oscillations with an external driving power with $50 \mathrm{~Hz}$ and a $V_m$ of $280 \mathrm{~V}$ is
questions.solution:
R=10 \Omega L=6 \mu $\mathrm{H},$C=10 \mu $\mathrm{H}$
Impedence of the circuit, Z=$\sqrt{R^2+\left(X_C-X_L\right)^2}$Capacitive reactance, $X_C=\frac{1}{\omega C}=\frac{1}{2 \pi f C}$ X_C=$\frac{1}{2 \times 314 \times 50 \times 10 \times 10^{-6}} =$318.47 \Omega Inductive reactance $X_L=\omega L=2 \pi f L\begin{aligned}$X_L & =2 $\times$314 $\times$50 $\times$6 $\times$10^{-6} \\ & =18.84 $\times$10^{-4} \Omega \end{aligned} Resistance, $R=10 \Omega\begin{gathered}$Z=$\sqrt{10^2+\left(318.4-18.84 \times 10^{-4}\right)^2}$\\ Z=$\sqrt{100+(318.39)^2}=\sqrt{101477.36}$\\ Z=318.55 \Omega \\ $\text { rms current, }$i_{\text {rms }}=$\frac{V_{\text {rms }}}{Z}=\frac{V_0 / \sqrt{2}}{Z}$\\ i_{\text {rms }}=$\frac{280}{\sqrt{2} \times 318.55}=$0.621 $\mathrm{~A} \end{gathered}$As energy is only dissipated in resistance as heat and no power dissipates in capacitor and inductor, so average power dissipates as heat $P=i_{\mathrm{rms}}^2 $\cdot$R $\begin{aligned}$ \text{ and } P=(0.621)^2 $\times$10 \\ \text{ and } P=3.8 $\mathrm{~W} \end{aligned}3.8 \mathrm{~W} power should be fed to maintain an undamped oscillation.

questions.q: A resistor $R=300 \Omega$ and a capacitor $C=25 \mu \mathrm{F}$ are connected in series with a $50 \mathrm{~V}, \frac{50}{\pi} \mathrm{Hz}$ AC source. The average power dissipated in the circuit is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text{Given,} R=300 \Omega, C=25 \mu \mathrm{F}=25 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~F} \\ & V=50 \mathrm{~V} \end{aligned}$ Frequency of AC source, $v=\frac{50}{\pi} \mathrm{Hz}\begin{array}{cc} \therefore$& 2 $\pi \nu=\omega$\\ \Rightarrow & $\omega=$2 $\pi \times \frac{50}{\pi}=$100 $\mathrm{rad}$/ $\mathrm{s} \end{array}\therefore$ AC voltage, $V=50 \cos \omega \mathrm{t}=50 \cos (100 t)\therefore$ rms voltage, $V_{\mathrm{rms}}=\frac{V_0}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{50}{\sqrt{2}}=25 \sqrt{2} \mathrm{~V}\therefore$ Impedance of the $R C$-circuit is $\begin{aligned}$Z & =$\sqrt{R^2+X_C^2}=\sqrt{R^2+\left(\frac{1}{\omega C}\right)^2}$\\ \therefore \quad Z & =$\sqrt{300^2+\left(\frac{1}{100 \times 25 \times 10^{-6}}\right)^2}$\\ & =$\sqrt{300^2+400^2}$\\ \Rightarrow \quad Z & =500 \Omega \end{aligned} $\therefore$ Current through the circuit, $I_{\mathrm{rms}}=\frac{V_{\mathrm{rms}}}{Z}$ =$\frac{25 \sqrt{2}}{500}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{20} \mathrm{~A}\therefore$ Average power dissipated through the circuit is $\begin{aligned}$< P> & =V_{\text {rms }} $\times$I_{\text {rms }} $\times \cos \phi$\\ & =25 $\sqrt{2} \times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{20} \times \frac{R}{Z}$\\ & =$\frac{50}{20} \times \frac{300}{500}=$1.5 $\mathrm{~W} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: An $AC$ circuit drawing power from a source of angular frequency $50rads^{- 1}$ has a power factor of $\text{0.6}$. In this condition, a resistance of $100Ω$ is present and the current is lagging behind the voltage. If a capacitor is connected in series, then the required capacitance that will result in a power factor of unity is
questions.solution:
As the current lags the voltage, the circuit must contain a combination of resistance and inductance.

Power factor $cos ⁡ ϕ = 0.6$

$⇒ \dfrac{R}{R^{2} + {X}_L^{2}} = \text{0.6}$

$⇒ R^{2} + {X}_L^{2} = \left(\dfrac{R}{0.6}\right)2$

$⇒ {X}_L^{2} = \dfrac{R2}{\left(\text{0.6}\right)2} - R^{2}$

$⇒ {X}_L^{2} = \dfrac{R^{2} \times \text{0.64}}{0.36}$

$∴ {X}_{L} = \dfrac{0 .8 R}{0 .6} = \dfrac{4R}{3}$

Now we want the power factor $cos ⁡ ϕ = 1$

This is the condition of resonance in which

${X}_{L} = {X}_{C}$

$∴ {X}_{C} = \dfrac{4R}{3}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{ωC} = \dfrac{4R}{3}$

$⇒ C = \dfrac{3}{4 \times 50 \times 100} = 150\mu F$

questions.solution: For a step-down transformer, \(\begin{aligned}N_P \text{ and } =5000, N_S=500 \\ I_P \text{ and } =4 $\mathrm{~A},$V_P=2200 $\mathrm{~V} \end{aligned}$\) For a transformer, we know that \$(\begin{aligned}$ \text{ and } $\frac{N_S}{N_P}=\frac{V_S}{V_P}=\frac{I_P}{I_S}$\\ \text{ and } $\text {Using, } \quad \frac{N_S}{N_P}=\frac{V_S}{V_P}$\\ \text{ and } \Rightarrow \quad V_S=$\frac{N_S V_P}{N_P}=\frac{500 \times 2200}{5000}=$220 $\mathrm{~V}$\\ \text{ and } $\text {Again, using } \frac{V_S}{V_P}=\frac{I_P}{I_S}$\\ \text{ and } I_S=$\frac{I_P \times V_P}{V_S}=\frac{4 \times 2200}{220}=$40 $\mathrm{~A}$\\ \end{aligned}\)$

questions.q: An AC source of angular frequency $\omega$ is fed across a resistor $R$ and a capacitor $C$ in series. The current flowing in the circuit found to be $I$. Now the frequency of the source is changed to $\frac{\omega}{3}$, (maintaining the same voltage) the current in the circuit is found to be halved. What is the ratio of reactance to resistance at the original frequency?
questions.solution: At angular frequency $\omega$, current through resistance R and capacitance C is given by $I_{\mathrm{rms}}=\frac{V_{\mathrm{rms}}}{\sqrt{R^2+X_C^2}}=\frac{V_{\mathrm{rms}}}{\sqrt{R^2+\left(\frac{1}{\omega C}\right)^2}}$...(i) When angular frequency is changed to $\frac{\omega}{3}$, then the current becomes $\frac{I_{\mathrm{rms}}}{2}=\frac{V_{\mathrm{rms}}}{\sqrt{R^2+\left(\frac{1}{\frac{\omega}{3} C}\right)^2}}=\frac{V_{\mathrm{rms}}}{\sqrt{R^2+\left(\frac{3}{\omega C}\right)^2}}...($ii) Dividing Eq. (i) by Eq. (ii), we get $\begin{array}{rlrl} & & 2=\frac{\sqrt{R^2+\left(\frac{3}{\omega C}\right)^2}}{\sqrt{R^2+ \left(\frac{1}{\omega C}\right)^2}}\\ \text{ and } \Rightarrow \text{ and } $4\l$left[R^2+\$left(\frac{1}{\omega C}\right)^2\right]$ \text{ and } $=R²+\left(\frac{3}{\omega C}\right)^2$\\ \text{ and } \Rightarrow \text{ and } 3 R² \text{ and } $=\frac{5}{\omega^2 C²}$\\ \text{ and } \Rightarrow \text{ and } $\frac{1}{\omega_C}$ \text{ and } $=\sqrt{\frac{3}{5}}$\\ \Rightarrow \text{ and } $\frac{X_C}{R}$ \text{ and } $=\sqrt{\frac{3}{5}}\end{array}$

questions.q: In a transformer the number of primary turns is four times that of the secondary turns. Its primary is connected to an AC source of voltage $V .$ Then
options: current through its secondary is about four times that of the current through its primary.
voltage across its secondary is about four times that of the voltage across its primary.
voltage across its secondary is about two times that of the voltage across the primary.
voltage across its secondary is about $\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}$ times of the voltage across its primary.
questions.solution:
In a transformer the primary and secondary currents are related by

${I}_{s} = \left(\dfrac{{N}_{p}}{{N}_{s}}\right){I}_{p}$

And the voltage are related by

${V}_{s} = \left(\dfrac{{N}_{s}}{{N}_{p}}\right){V}_{p}$

Where subscripts p and s refer to the primary and secondary of the transformer.

Here, ${V}_{p} = V, \dfrac{{N}_{p}}{{N}_{s}} = 4$

$∴ {I}_{s} = 4{I}_{p}$

And ${V}_{s} = \left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)V = \dfrac{V}{4}$

questions.q: The average power output of a point source of an electromagnetic radiation is $1080 \mathrm{~W}$. The maximum value of the rms value of the electric field at a distance of $3 \mathrm{~m}$ from the source is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Maximum emf, } \varepsilon_0=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{P}}{2 \pi \mathrm{R}^2 \mathrm{E}_0 \mathrm{c}}} \\ & =\sqrt{\frac{1080}{2 \times 3.14 \times 3^2 \times 8.85 \times 10^{-12} \times 3 \times 10^8}} \\ & =\sqrt{\frac{1080 \times 10^8}{54 \times 314 \times 885}=84.85} \\ & \therefore \varepsilon_{\mathrm{rms}}=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{84.85}{1.414} \simeq 60 \mathrm{Vm}^{-1}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: What is the value of inductance $L$ for which the current is a maximum in a series $L C R$ circuit with $C=10 \mu \mathrm{F}$ and $\omega=1000 \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$ ?
options: Cannot be calculated unless $R$ is known
questions.solution: Current in $L C R$ series circuit, $i=\frac{V}{\sqrt{R^{2}+\left(X_{L}-X_{C}\right)^{2}}}$ where $V$ is rms value of current, $R$ is resistance, $X_{L}$ is inductive reactance and $X_{C}$ is capacitive reactance. For current to be maximum, denominator should be minimum which can be done, if X_{L}=X_{C} This happens in resonance state of the circuit ie, $\omega$L=$\frac{1}{\omega C}$or $\quad L=\frac{1}{\omega^{2} C}$ ...(i) $\begin{aligned} \text { Given, } \omega &=1000 \mathrm{~s}^{-1}, C=10 \mu \mathrm{F} \\ &=10 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~F} \\ \text { Hence, } L &=\frac{1}{(1000)^{2} \times 10 \times 10^{-6}} \\ &=0.1 \mathrm{H} \\ &=100 \mathrm{mH} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: A current of $5A$ is flowing at $220V$ in the primary coil of a transformer. If the voltage produced in the secondary coil is $2200V$ and $50%$ of power is lost, then the current in the secondary coil is
questions.solution:
Given, power output

$= \dfrac{1}{2} \times$ power input (or $50%$ of input power)

$∴ {I}_{s}{V}_{s} = \dfrac{1}{2}{I}_{p} ⋅ {V}_{p} \left[∵ P = VI\right]$

Here, ${I}_{p} = 5A, {V}_{p} = 220V$

and ${V}_{s} = 2200V$

$∴ {I}_{s} = $\dfrac{{I}_{p} ⋅ {V}_{p}}{2{V}_{s}} = \dfrac{5 \times 220}{2 \times 2200} =$0.25A$

questions.q: An ac voltage of $10 \sin \omega t$ volt is applied to a pure inducfor of inductance $10 \mathrm{H}$. The current through the inductor in ampere is
questions.solution: Apply the kirchhoff's loop rule $\begin{aligned}$& V+E=0 \\ & V-L $\frac{d i}{d t}=$0 \\ & V=L $\frac{d i}{d t} \end{aligned} \begin{aligned}$& $\frac{\mathrm{di}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\frac{\mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{L}}=\mathrm{V}}_{0} $\frac{\sin \omega \mathrm{t}}{\mathrm{L}}$\\ \text{ and } \$mathrm{di}=\frac{\mathrm{V}_0}{\mathrm{~L}} \sin \omega \mathrm{t} \end{aligned}$Integration with respect to time $t\begin{aligned}$ \text{ and } $i=\frac{V_0}{L}\left(-\frac{\cos \omega t}{\omega}\right)=\frac{-V_0}{\omega L} \cos \omega$t \\ \text{ and } $i=\frac{V_0}{\omega L} \sin \left(\omegat-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\frac{10}{\omega \times 10} \sin \left(\omegat-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$\\ & $i=\frac{1}{\omega} \sin \left(\omegat-\frac{\pi}{2}\right) \end{aligned}$

questions.q: A resistor of resistance of $100 \Omega$ is connected to an AC source $\varepsilon=10 \sin \left(250 \pi \mathrms^{-1}\right) \mathrm{t}$. The energy dissipated as heat during $\mathrm{t}=0$ to $\mathrm{t}=1 \mathrm{~ms}$ is approximately.
questions.solution: Given that $\varepsilon=10 \sin \left(250 \pi \mathrms^{-}\right) \mathrm{t}$ Compair with $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_0 \sin (\omega \mathrm{t})\omega=250 \pi \mathrm{Rad} / \mathrm{s}$ The energy dissipated as $\begin{aligned}$& $\mathrm{H}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}} \int_0^{10^{-3}} \varepsilon_0^2 \sin ^2 $\omega \mathrm{tdt}$\\  \text{ and }  =$\frac{\varepsilon_0^2}{2 \mathrm{R}} \int_0^{10^{-3}}(1-\cos 2 $\omega \mathrm{t}) \mathrm{dt}$\\ & =$\frac{\varepsilon_0^2}{2 \mathrm{R}}\left[\mathrm{t}-\frac{\sin 2 \omega \mathrm{t}}{2 \omega}\right]^{10^{-3}}$\\ & =$\frac{\varepsilon_0^2}{2 \mathrm{R}}\left[$10^{-3}-$\frac{\sin 2 \times 250 \pi}{2 \times 250 \pi} \times$10^{-3}\right] \\ & $=\frac{100}{2 \times 100} \lleft[10^{-3}-\frac{1}{500 \pi}\right]$\\ & $=\frac{1}{2}  \left[\frac{1}{1000}-\frac{1}{500 \pi}\right]=\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{\pi-2}{1000 \pi}\right]$\\ \text{ and } $=\frac{0.57}{\pi} \mathrm{mJ} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: A resistor of resistance $\mathrm{R}$ and an inductor of inductive reactance $\mathrm{R}$ are connected in series to an ac source. A capacitor of capacitive reactance $2 \mathrm{R}$ is then connected in series with $L$ and $R$. The ratio of the power fators of $L R$ and LCR circuits is
questions.solution: Power factor of LCR circuit is $\begin{aligned} \mathrm{P}_1=\cos \phi & =\frac{\mathrm{R}}{\sqrt{\mathrm{R}^2+\left(\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}-\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{C}}\right)^2}}=\frac{\mathrm{R}}{\sqrt{\mathrm{R}^2+(2 \mathrm{R}-\mathrm{R})^2}} \\ & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \end{aligned}$ Power factor of L R circuit is $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{P}_2=\frac{\mathrm{R}}{\sqrt{\mathrm{R}^2+\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}^2}}=\frac{\mathrm{R}}{\sqrt{\mathrm{R}^2+\mathrm{R}^2}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ & \text { Ratio }=\frac{\mathrm{P}_2}{\mathrm{P}_1}=\frac{1}{1}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: In an AC circuit, the instantaneous values of emf and current are $E = 200sin\left(300t\right)V$ and $i = 2sin ⁡ \left(300t + \dfrac{π}{3}\right)A$ respectively. The average power consumed (in $W$) is
questions.solution:
The average power consumed in an AC circuit is given by

$P = \dfrac{{V}_{0}{I}_{0}}{2}cos ⁡ ϕ$

Where $ϕ$ is phase angle and ${V}_{0}$ and ${I}_{0}$ are the peak values of voltage and current respectively.

Given, ${V}_{0} = 200V, {I}_{0} = 2A, ϕ = \dfrac{π}{3}$.

$P = \dfrac{200 \times 2}{2}cos ⁡ \dfrac{π}{3}$

$= \dfrac{200 \times 2}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 100W$

questions.q: A telephone wire of length $200$ km has a capacitance of $0.014\muF$ per $\text{km}$. If it carries an AC frequency $5kHz,$ what should be the value of an inductor required to be connected in series so that the impedance of the circuit is minimum?
questions.solution:
Capacitance of wire

$C = 0.014 \times {10}^{- 6} \times 200$

$= 2.8 \times {10}^{- 6}F = 2.8\mu F$

For impedance of the circuit to be minimum

${X}_{L} = {X}_{C}$

$⇒ 2\pifL = \dfrac{1}{2\pifC}$

$L = \dfrac{1}{4{\pi}^{2}f^{2}C}$

$= \dfrac{1}{4{\left(3.14\right)}^{2} \times {\left(5 \times {10}^{3}\right)}^{2} \times 2.8 \times {10}^{- 6}}$

$= 0.35 \times {10}^{- 3}H = 0.35mH$

questions.q: The instantaneous current and voltage of an AC circuit are given by $i = 10sin\left(314t\right)A$ and $V = 100sin\left(314t\right)V$. What is the power dissipation in the circuit?
questions.solution:
Given,

$I = 10sin\left(314t\right)A$ and $V = 100sin\left(314t\right)V$

Comparing with $I = {I}_{0}sin \omega t$ and $V = {V}_{0}sin \omega t$,we get

$∴ {I}_{0} = 10\text{A}$ and ${V}_{0} = 100\text{V}$

$\begin{array}{ll}⇒ {I}_{rms} = \dfrac{10}{2}\text{A,}{V}_{rms} = \dfrac{100}{2}\text{V,} \\ \text{Phase difference}ϕ{=0}^{o} \\ ∴ \text{Power dissipated}{P}_{av} = {V}_{rms} \times {I}_{rms} \times cosϕ \\ = ( \dfrac{10}{2} )( \dfrac{100}{2} )cos{0}^{o} \\ = 500\text{W}\end{array}$

questions.q: An inductor coil takes current $8 \mathrm{~A}$ when connected to a $100 \mathrm{~V}$ and $50 \mathrm{~Hz} \mathrm{AC}$ source. A pure resistor under the same condition takes current of $10 \mathrm{~A}$. If inductor coil and resistor are connected in series to a $100 \mathrm{~V}$ and $40 \mathrm{~Hz}$ AC supply, then the current in the series combination of above resistor and inductor is
questions.solution: Inductive reactance when $100 \mathrm{~V}, 50 \mathrm{~Hz}$ source is connected is given by $\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}=\frac{\mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{I}}=\frac{100}{8}=$12.5 \Omega Resistance $\mathrm{R}=\frac{\mathrm{V}}{1}=\frac{100}{10}=10 \Omega$ Inductive reactance at new frequency of $40 \mathrm{~Hz}\begin{aligned}$& $\frac{\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}^{\prime}}{\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}}=\frac{2 \pi \mathrmf^{\prime} \mathrm{L}}{2 \pi \mathrm{fL}}=\frac{40}{50}=\frac{4}{5}$\\ & $\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}^{\prime}=\frac{4}{5} \mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}=\frac{4}{5} \times$12.5=10 \Omega \end{aligned} When they are connected in series the impedance will be given by $\begin{aligned}$& Z=$\sqrt{R^2+X_L^{\prime 2}}=\sqrt{(10)^2+(10)^2}=$10 $\sqrt{2}$A \\ & I=$\frac{V}{Z}=\frac{100}{10 \sqrt{2}}=$5 $\sqrt{2} \mathrm{~A} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: In the adjacent circuit, the instantaneous current equation is
questions.solution:
Let $ϕ$ is the phase difference between $V$ and $i$

$\text\tan ⁡ ϕ = \dfrac{XL}{R} = \dfrac{\omegaL}{R} = \dfrac{100 \times 1}{100} =1$

$⇒ ϕ = \dfrac{π}{4}$

Since this is an $LR$ circuit, $V$ will lead $i$

$∴$ The instantaneous current equation will be

${i}_{} = {i}_{0}\text\sin ⁡ \left(100t - ϕ\right)$ where $ϕ = $\dfrac{π}{4}and ${i}_{0} = $\dfrac{V0}{Z}

${i}_{0} = $\dfrac{V0}{R^{2} + \left(\omegaL\right)2} = \dfrac{200}{\left(100\right)2 + \left(100 \times 1\right)2} = $\sqrt{2}$

$∴ i = \sqrt{2}\text\sin⁡ \left(100t - \dfrac{π}{4}\right)$
